points.description: States that a prototype program simulates / imitates / models the behaviour (functionality) of the desired software product. Equivalent wording such as 'mimics how the final system will work' or 'a working model of the product' earns the mark.

levels.says: Describes a prototype as an early, trial or sample version of the software, but does not say it simulates or models the behaviour or functionality of the product.

points.description: States that the prototype simulates only portions / parts / key features of the product (for example the user interface or a risky module), not the whole finished product.

levels.says: Implies a partial or simplified version (for example 'rough', 'basic' or 'limited') without clearly saying it covers only portions of the product.

points.description: Gives the purpose in problem solving: used to explore, test or clarify requirements and design, get user or client feedback, or find problems or risks early before the final software is built. Any one such valid purpose earns the mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks need: simulates the behaviour of the product, only for portions of it, and a valid purpose (testing ideas, getting feedback, early problem detection). The model answer alone earns P1 and P2 in full (4 marks); the fifth mark is for a purpose. Vague answers like 'a first version' earn part marks only.

selftest_notes: The model answer scored only 4 of 5.
